title: Launch safety playbook: release blockers, rollback runbook, and comms templates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a single operational playbook that coordinates release blockers, a tested rollback runbook, and standardized incident communications for the runtime-1.20 launch. Goal: reduce go/no-go ambiguity, shorten mean-time-to-decision during incidents, and ensure cross-team readiness for production-facing regressions.
checklist: Finalize release notes draft and owner mapping (PM -> Engineering reviewer -> Documentation) - GH: draft in docs/release_notes/runtime-1.20.md
Complete preflight checklist for Dedicated/Dedicated-Beta capacity (capacity smoke tests + quota verification)
Verify observability: trace hooks, synthetic latency tests, billing tags present in telemetry
Confirm rollback automation: infra script exists and tested in staging (PR #3456)
Run canned canary traffic and validate QPS/latency SLOs for top 5 customer flows
Obtain sign-off from Security and Compliance on KMS integration changes
Publish incident communication templates and run tabletop with cross-functional reps
release_blockers: Open performance regression >10% P95 compared to runtime-1.19 on critical path (blocking until mitigated or plan accepted)
Any data-plane schema change without migration strategy documented and validated
Failed Dedicated autoscaler test (sustained tail latency spike >300ms under load)
Unreviewed security findings classified as High or Critical
Missing owner for release notes or no documented release timeline for customer-facing comms
rollback_plan: Trigger condition: sustained error-rate increase >1.5x baseline for 10 minutes OR P95 latency regressions exceeding 2x SLA for 5 minutes
Immediate action: PM declares 'Rollback Intent' on #launch-runtime and notifies Oncall and SRE
Step 1: Disable new model routing via routing-policy toggle (console toggle ID: rp-rt-120)
Step 2: Re-route traffic to previous runtime tag runtime-1.19 via Smart Router (playbook command: router rollback runtime-1.19)
Step 3: If automated rollback fails, execute infra rollback script (repo: infra/deploy-scripts/rollback_runtime.sh) with SRE lead
Step 4: Run validation smoke tests (health checks, sample convo run, embedding hashing) and confirm metrics have returned to baseline
Step 5: Postmortem ownership assigned within 24 hours and customer-impact assessment within 48 hours
incident_comm_templates: Internal alert (Slack): [{{incident_id}}] Runtime-1.20 degraded - TL;DR: increased 5xx rate on inference path. Current action: routing rollback initiated. Owners: Marcus Liu (PM), Priya Kapoor (SRE). See runbook: <confluence://runbooks/runtime-1.20>.

Customer status (public page): Incident {{incident_id}} impacting inference latency for a subset of requests to Model X. We are actively investigating and have initiated rollback to the prior runtime version. Next update: in 30 minutes. Contact: support@redwood.ai for urgent escalations.

Customer email template (for affected accounts): Subject: Service incident impacting inference latency - {{incident_id}}. Body: We detected a regression in runtime-1.20 affecting latency. We have rolled back to runtime-1.19 and are monitoring. No customer data was exposed. Full postmortem will be shared within 72 hours. Support link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/{{incident_id}}

External social post (short): We experienced an incident affecting inference latency today and rolled back changes. No customer data impact. More details: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/{{incident_id}}
go_no_go_criteria: All P0 release blockers cleared or accepted with mitigation and owner
Smoke tests green for 30 minutes under canary traffic with no cold-start regressions
Rollback validated in staging and dry-run completed by SRE and Infra leads
Release notes reviewed and approved by Documentation + Legal (links attached)
Customer-facing comms templates approved and localized where required

notes: Trade-off: If we accept a temporary 5% cost increase for 48 hours we can enable more aggressive KV cache warming to reduce tail latency; SRE prefers a configuration toggle rather than permanent change.
